title: Cases of Working Adults Who Face Short-term Family Support Challenges
what_it_is: Cases of Working Adults Who Face Short-term Family Support Challenges

sections.label: Infant, childcare and parent leave
sections.summary: Each parent can take six days of infant care leave yearly for children under two, six days of childcare leave if the youngest child is under seven, and two days if aged 7 to 12.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To attend to childcare needs, each parent can tap on six days of infant care leave per year for children below two years old, another six days of childcare leave per year if their youngest child is below seven years old, and two days per year if their youngest child is aged 7 to 12.

sections.label: Tripartite standards and caregiver support
sections.summary: MOM introduced tripartite standards on flexible work arrangements and unpaid leave for unexpected care needs, provides Work-life Grant funding, and reviewed caregiver support with MOH and MSF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In the last two years, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) introduced the Tripartite Standard on Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) to encourage employers to offer FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MOM also introduced the Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs to encourage employers to provide employees with additional leave support during unexpected caregiving exigencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: MOM also provides funding support to employers for the sustained adoption of FWAs through the Work-life Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In this aspect, the Ministry of Health (MOH), together with MOM and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), have undertaken a review to strengthen support for caregivers of seniors.

sections.label: Respite care for seniors
sections.summary: MOH is currently looking into enhancing the provision of respite care for parents with seniors at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Indeed, these are issues that we have been looking at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: So, for example, for the respite care for parents with seniors at home, I understand that MOH is currently looking into enhancing the provision of respite care.

sections.label: Addressing urgent ad hoc childcare needs
sections.summary: They will work and discuss with agencies under the Ministry and community partners to find a solution for parents' ad hoc and urgent childcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: That has also strengthened our resolve in reviewing this and to come up with some solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: So, we will be working and discussing with the agencies under the Ministry as well as with community partners to find a solution to address the childcare needs on an ad hoc and urgent basis by the parents.

sections.label: Employment matters with MOM
sections.summary: The matter concerns employment matters and will have to be studied together with MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: And it is also something concerning employment matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: So, we will have to study it together with MOM.
